sections.h2: Myrtle Beach housing at a glance
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach sits in Horry County on the Grand Strand. The city had 35,682 residents in the 2020 census and an estimate of 40,937 for 2025. Homes range from older cottages near the oceanfront to much newer condos and subdivisions further inland, with a median build year of 1992.

A house here may be a primary home, a retiree's place or a short-term rental, and the tax treatment is different for each. Owners who depend on seasonal work or rental income also feel the January 15 bill, which lands at a slow point in the year.

sections.h2: Coastal condition and what buyers check
sections.html:
Hurricanes are the main risk on this coast. Salt air, wind-driven rain and flooding are what a buyer's inspector looks at first: roof covering, windows, siding, HVAC and crawl-space moisture.

A house with deferred storm repairs can be hard to finance, and that is one reason owners choose a cash sale. Check your insurance and flood status before listing, because the answers affect what buyers can borrow.

sections.h2: Who bills Myrtle Beach property tax and where to pay
sections.html:
The Horry County Treasurer collects real property tax for Myrtle Beach addresses. Notices go to the owner of record, and city, county and school district taxes all appear on the same bill. The Treasurer has four offices:

  • Conway (main): 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, SC 29526
  • Myrtle Beach: 332 Hinson Dr, Myrtle Beach, SC 29579
  • South Strand: 9630 Scipio Lane, Surfside, SC 29588
  • Stephen's Crossroads: 107 Hwy 57 North, Little River, SC 29566

Hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the main number is (843) 915-5470. You can pay in person, by mail, in the night deposit box, online, or by phone at 843-428-2126. Card payments carry convenience fees.

For exemptions and address changes on real property, call the Tax Assessor at (843) 915-5040. Homestead questions go to the Auditor at (843) 915-5051.

Payment is due in full on or before January 15 of the year after the tax year. A bill postmarked later picks up penalties in three steps under S.C. Code 12-45-180. Not receiving a bill does not excuse a penalty.

Payment datePenalty added
January 163 percent
February 27 percent more
March 175 percent more, then tax execution

Horry County also has an installment payment program, and the Treasurer holds an annual public tax sale for delinquent properties. Ask the Treasurer for the sale date and for the installment terms.

sections.h2: Why second homes and rentals in Myrtle Beach pay more
sections.html:
A house that is not a legal residence is assessed at 6 percent of fair market value instead of 4 percent. A home rented more than 72 days a year does not qualify for the 4 percent ratio.

The city has promoted a tax calculator, maintained by the Myrtle Beach Area Chamber of Commerce at mbtaxcalc.com. It describes a Tourism Development Fee credit for primary homeowners inside the city. That credit applies to owner-occupied homes only, so call the county for your actual figures.

The gap matters at sale time. An investor selling a vacation rental and an owner selling a primary home carry different bills, and a buyer who plans to live in the house must apply for the 4 percent ratio before the first penalty date.

sections.h2: Selling a Myrtle Beach house when you owe tax
sections.html:
You can sell. The title company pays the Horry County balance from your proceeds at closing, as long as the price covers it. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer first, because penalties change on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

Here is the usual order of steps:

  • Call the Treasurer for the balance and a payoff good through your expected closing date.
  • Ask whether the property has been advertised for the annual tax sale.
  • Give the payoff letter to the title company so it can be paid at the table.
  • Confirm with the Auditor or Assessor how the legal residence status is recorded, since the buyer's bill depends on it.

If a tax sale happens before you sell, S.C. Code 12-51-90 lets the owner redeem within twelve months. Interest is 3 percent of the bid in months one to three, 6 in months four to six, 9 in months seven to nine, and 12 in months ten to twelve. Selling before the sale avoids that clock entirely.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance without waiting on a lender's appraisal or repair list, which helps when a storm-worn house or a deadline is the problem.

If you disagree with the value, send a written objection to the assessor within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed. That deadline comes from S.C. Code 12-60-2510.

Gather what supports your case before you write: recent sale prices nearby, repair estimates, photos of damage and a copy of the notice. Call the Tax Assessor at (843) 915-5040 if you are unsure which form to file.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Myrtle Beach?
faqs.a: Horry County does. The Treasurer has an office at 332 Hinson Drive in Myrtle Beach and the main office at 1301 Second Avenue in Conway.

faqs.q: When is Myrtle Beach property tax due?
faqs.a: It is due on or before January 15. Penalties start on January 16, then February 2 and March 17.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Myrtle Beach property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. Horry County accepts online payment by check or Visa, MasterCard or Discover. Card payments carry convenience fees.

faqs.q: Do rentals in Myrtle Beach get the 4 percent rate?
faqs.a: Not if the home is rented more than 72 days a year. State law then treats it as other real property at 6 percent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Myrtle Beach house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, as long as the price covers it. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure.
